展示会.quote: Industrial 3D Printing: Formnext 2026 Showcases Growth Markets and Scalable Business Models - PolyForm NEXT

Despite the challenging economic environment, additive manufacturing is increasingly evolving into an industrially scalable technology that opens the door to new business models and growth markets. Formnext 2026, taking place November 17–20 in Frankfurt, will showcase just how far this development has come.

Formnext 2026 will bring together key players in the additive manufacturing industry in Frankfurt from November 17 to 20. About 800 exhibitors are expected to attend. The event will focus on industrial applications, new business models, post-processing, and growth sectors such as aerospace, defense, energy, medical, and semiconductors.

The debate on industrial development in Europe and around the world is currently dominated by economic challenges. But there is another trend: Numerous examples show how additive manufacturing enables successful and scalable business models in industrial applications—and thereby opens up new growth markets.

Formnext, taking place in Frankfurt from November 17 to 20, 2026, aims to highlight precisely this trend. The trade show brings together relevant technologies and experts in one place. The focus is on concrete applications across the entire value chain, as well as application examples and business cases from various industries.

Additive manufacturing can provide concrete solutions to these challenges. It helps companies respond more quickly to changes, develop new applications, and strengthen their competitiveness in the long term.

Against this backdrop, Formnext sees itself as the central platform for the manufacturing technologies of the future in 2026 as well. Approximately 800 exhibitors are expected to attend. This will ensure that relevant companies from across the entire AM ecosystem are represented.

“Especially in the current market climate, it’s clear just how important dialogue, guidance, and access to innovation are,” explains Sascha F. Wenzler, Vice President of Formnext at the event organizer
. “Formnext brings together key players and creates a framework in which new ideas for the industrial application of additive manufacturing can emerge.”

According to Formnext, the outlook for the industry is now more positive as well. Discussions with the Formnext Exhibitor Advisory Board indicate that sentiment in many sectors is significantly better than in previous years.
Highlighting these developments and fostering discussion about them is therefore one of Formnext's most important tasks.
Three halls instead of four levels
The trade show is also changing in terms of layout. The organizer has further optimized the hall layout for the upcoming edition.
Instead of four hall levels, Halls 11.0, 12.0, and 12.1 will be used. The total exhibition space is not expected to be significantly reduced.
The supporting program for Formnext 2026 will also feature a wide variety of topics. It is designed to offer opportunities for both in-depth professional learning and networking.
Among other things, the Formnext Defense Summit is setting new priorities in terms of content. It highlights current developments and requirements in the security and defense sectors.

In addition, tried-and-true formats will remain in place. The Formnext Awards will once again recognize outstanding innovations and developments. The Discover3DPrinting seminars are designed to provide beginners, in particular, with a hands-on introduction to additive manufacturing.
